name: LiteLLM
description: An OpenAI-compatible gateway in front of a hundred model providers: one base URL and one key for every application, with per-key budgets, spend logs and an admin UI. Models and keys are kept in the PostgreSQL database on a private network beside it.

access.note: The admin UI at https://<domain>/ui signs in with the user named here and the password generated here; reveal it from the Variables tab. Applications authenticate with the master key instead, which LiteLLM requires to start with "sk-": it is "sk-" followed by the generated master-key value. Models and their provider keys are added from the UI and stored encrypted in the database, so nothing here holds a provider's key.

inputs.name: domain
inputs.label: Public domain
inputs.description: Optional; the address applications and the UI are reached at. LiteLLM builds no absolute URLs, so nothing else here changes when it is set.

secrets.name: ui-password
secrets.label: UI admin password
secrets.description: Reveal it from the Variables tab to sign in to /ui.

secrets.name: master-key
secrets.label: Master key (after the sk- prefix)
secrets.description: The master key applications send is "sk-" followed by this value. It also mints every other virtual key.

secrets.name: salt-key
secrets.label: Salt key (after the sk- prefix)
secrets.description: Encrypts provider keys stored in the database; LiteLLM says never to change it once models exist.

secrets.name: db-password
secrets.label: Database password
secrets.description: Generated here and given only to the services that sign in to the database.

services.name: litellm
services.purpose: The proxy, the admin UI and the key API, behind the domain

ports.name: http
ports.purpose: The OpenAI-compatible API and the admin UI

services.name: db
services.purpose: PostgreSQL, holding models, virtual keys, teams and spend logs

automation.name: Nightly backup
automation.description: Archives every volume of the stack every night.

update.notes: LiteLLM migrates its database on start. Keep the salt key: provider keys stored in the database are encrypted with it and cannot be read with another.
